creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`View::step` walks only the regions on screen (`composition/view.rs`), so a pane in a tab no region is showing cannot be reached by any chord. Clicking its row in the sidebar is the only door, and it is now a door that can be closed: putting the list away (a_28NRKvB12) leaves those panes with no way in at all.

Muster has next/previous and four directions, and between them they guarantee reaching every pane **the window is showing**. What is missing is the other axis - the tabs behind the ones on screen. Ghostty has ⌘1..⌘9 for this and most terminals have something.

Worth deciding rather than defaulting:

- **What the numbers count.** Tabs of the focused region's daemon? Every tab across every attached daemon, in roster order? The second is more useful in a two-machine window and harder to hold in your head.
- **Whether it is numbers at all.** The roster is already ordered and labelled by the core, so `focus_next_tab`/`focus_previous_tab` over that order is one pair of chords instead of nine, and does not go stale when a tab closes.
- **What it does to the region.** `FocusPane` already surfaces a hidden pane by retargeting a region, so the machinery exists; this is about naming the destination, not about getting there.
title: ⌨️ A hidden tab is reachable by mouse and nothing else
